notes.meaning: God removed Moses' fears by giving him divine authority to speak and act in His name before Pharaoh. Aaron was appointed as Moses' spokesman, just as prophets deliver God's words to the people. Moses was not appearing as an ordinary beggar, but as God's official representative who held power over the king.

The Lord established a clear line of communication for this mission. Moses was to pass every command from God to Aaron, and Aaron was to boldly deliver the message to Pharaoh. Neither brother had the right to water down God's words or reduce the demand to set Israel free.

God told Moses ahead of time that Pharaoh would stubbornly resist, which would open the way for the Lord to perform many miracles across Egypt. These wonders would put God's supreme power on display before the entire nation. Even when evil leaders rebel, God remains in complete control of the outcome.

differ.view: God actively hardened Pharaoh's heart as a just judgment, sovereignly using Pharaoh's stubbornness to display His glory and power.
God did not cause Pharaoh to sin, but permitted Pharaoh's already rebellious heart to harden by withholding restraint in response to the divine commands.

notes.meaning: Because Pharaoh would refuse to listen, the Lord planned to strike Egypt with powerful acts of judgment. God promised to lead the Israelites out of slavery in orderly divisions, just like an organized army. Human defiance cannot stop God from rescuing His people.

When the Lord stretched out His hand against Egypt, the Egyptians would finally realize that He alone is the true God. The gods of Egypt would be exposed as powerless and false. In the end, God will make His authority known to the entire world.

Moses and Aaron set aside their earlier hesitation and obeyed the Lord completely. They carried out every instruction without arguing or trying to change the plan. True faith shows itself in steady and exact obedience.

Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they stood before Pharaoh. Their advanced age showed that this rescue did not depend on youthful energy, but on God's strength supporting them. God can use His servants to do great work at any stage of life.

God told His messengers what to expect when they met Pharaoh. Knowing the king would demand a sign to prove they came from God, the Lord told Aaron to throw down his staff, which would miraculously become a serpent.

Moses and Aaron entered the royal court and followed God's orders precisely. Aaron threw his staff onto the ground in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it instantly turned into a serpent. God graciously provided clear proof of His power before sending any painful plagues.

Pharaoh summoned his court sorcerers and magicians to see if they could match Aaron's miracle. Using secret arts and demonic deception, they threw down their staffs and appeared to produce the same result. Evil powers often try to mimic the truth in order to keep people in spiritual blindness.

Even though the magicians produced serpents, Aaron's staff swallowed up all of theirs. This showed clearly that the God of Israel had total authority over the occult arts and gods of Egypt. God's truth will always triumph over every false power.

Despite seeing his magicians thoroughly beaten, Pharaoh remained stubborn and refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. His hard reaction happened exactly as the Lord had predicted. A prideful heart will make excuses even when faced with clear evidence.

The Lord told Moses that Pharaoh's heart was totally unyielding and fixed in rebellion. Because the king refused to let the people go, Egypt would now face severe consequences. God knows the condition of every human heart before judgment begins.

God told Moses to confront Pharaoh the next morning by the edge of the Nile River, where the king went out to bathe or perform religious devotions. Moses was to carry the staff that had turned into a serpent as a visible reminder of God's authority. God meets sinners directly where they place their false trust.

Moses was instructed to deliver God's straightforward demand to let His people go to worship Him in the wilderness. He was also to point out that Pharaoh had willfully ignored every warning up to that moment. God's call to repentance is always clear and without compromise.

God announced that Pharaoh would finally come to know the Lord through what was about to happen. By striking the Nile with Aaron's staff, the Lord would turn the river water into real blood. God directly targeted the river that the Egyptians worshipped as the source of their life.

Turning the river into blood would bring immediate ruin to the country. The fish would die, the water would rot with a sickening smell, and the Egyptians would be unable to drink from their prized river. What people turn into an idol often becomes the very thing that brings them misery.

Aaron was commanded to stretch his staff over all the waters of Egypt, including the streams, canals, ponds, and domestic reservoirs. The disaster was so complete that even the water stored in wooden buckets and stone jars inside people's homes would turn to blood. When God brings judgment, no corner of life is out of His reach.

Moses and Aaron carried out God's orders right in front of Pharaoh and his royal court. Aaron lifted the staff and struck the Nile, and all the water turned into blood before their eyes. God worked this miracle out in the open so that no one could claim it was a secret trick.

Every part of God's warning took place just as He had said. The fish died, the air filled with an unbearable stench, and there was blood across the entire land of Egypt. The nation was instantly deprived of its basic need for clean water.

The Egyptian magicians managed to copy the plague on a small scale by turning a bit of fresh water red through their magic arts. Instead of using their powers to clean the river and help the people, their trick only gave Pharaoh an excuse to keep his heart hard. Satan's deceptions only add to human suffering rather than curing it.

Pharaoh turned his back on the ruined river, walked into his palace, and refused to take God's warning seriously. His pride kept him from caring about the terrible distress falling on his kingdom. Ignoring God's correction only leads to deeper judgment.

Because the river was completely undrinkable, ordinary Egyptians had to dig holes in the sand along the banks to search for groundwater. Even while sending judgment, God showed mercy by allowing them to find just enough water to survive. God's justice is often tempered with kindness toward those caught in the middle.

This terrible plague lasted for seven full days before it was lifted. During that entire week, Pharaoh was too proud to ask Moses to pray to the Lord for relief. Delaying repentance only causes unnecessary pain to last longer.
